abstract:
Lysine crotonylation (LCR) is an emerging post-translational modification, yet its clinical significance and therapeutic relevance in clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) remain poorly understood.
Multi-omics data were collected from public repositories. Consensus clustering based on 18 LCR-related genes (LCRGs) was performed to define molecular subtypes. Co-expression modules identified via WGCNA were integrated into 101 machine-learning combinations to establish a LCR-related signature (LCRS). The signature was evaluated for survival prediction, immune microenvironment characteristics, and drug response across multiple cohorts, complemented by single-cell RNA sequencing. Candidate therapeutic targets and compounds were screened using DepMap CRISPR dependency data and pharmacogenomic databases (CTRP and PRISM).
Two distinct molecular subtypes (C1 and C2) were identified, displaying significant differences in survival, immune infiltration, and signaling pathways. Integrating WGCNA hub genes with an optimal machine-learning framework yielded a robust 15-gene LCRS, which served as an independent prognostic factor in the TCGA cohorts. Single-cell analysis localized signature genes predominantly to endothelial cells. Pharmacogenomic profiling indicated higher sensitivity to sunitinib among high-risk patients, whereas low-risk patients displayed elevated sensitivity to axitinib and pazopanib. Furthermore, dependency screening prioritized CLCNKA as a key therapeutic target along with ten candidate compounds for high-risk patients.
This study establishes a robust LCR-related prognostic signature and nominates CLCNKA as a novel therapeutic vulnerability, offering actionable insights for personalized stratification and treatment in ccRCC.

summary: Builds a 15-gene lysine crotonylation prognostic signature in ccRCC from public multi-omics via WGCNA and 101 ML combinations; nominates CLCNKA as a target.
title: Integrated single-cell and bulk RNA-Seq analysis reveals a LCR-related prognostic signature for precision prognostication and therapeutic stratification in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
